rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone controls dominion, giving or removing it and granting honor or humiliation; whatever He wills occurs, and what He does not will cannot occur.
rows.anchor: أنت المعطي، وأنت المانع، وأنت الذي ما شئت كان وما لم تشأ لم يكن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse directs the Prophet and Muslim community to thank God for transferring prophethood from Israel to the Arab Qurashi Meccan unlettered final messenger, distinguished by many gifts and a worldwide mission.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية تنبيه وإرشاد إلى شكر نعمة الله تعالى على رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers those who presume to choose the recipient of revelation: He apportions mercy and worldly livelihood as He wills, and chooses where to place His message.
rows.anchor: أي: نحن نتصرف في خلقنا كما نريد، بلا ممانع ولا مدافع

rows.speaker: المأمون الخليفة
rows.claim: Ibn Asakir reports that al-Ma'mun saw a Himyaritic inscription in a Roman-land palace saying night, day, and the stars' course accompany kingdoms changing hands, while the Lord of the Throne's kingdom endures.
rows.anchor: عن المأمون الخليفة: أنه رأى في قصر ببلاد الروم مكتوبا بالحميرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes night enter day and day enter night by lengthening one as the other shortens, so they alternate between balance and difference through the seasons.
rows.anchor: تأخذ من طول هذا فتزيده في قصر هذا فيعتدلان، ثم تأخذ من هذا في هذا فيتفاوتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living includes seeds and plants, palms and date stones, believers and unbelievers, and eggs and chickens.
rows.anchor: تخرج الحبة من الزرع والزرع من الحبة، والنخلة من النواة والنواة من النخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives some people wealth beyond counting and restricts others, according to His wisdom, will, choice, and justice.
rows.anchor: تعطي من شئت من المال ما لا يعده ولا يقدر على إحصائه، وتقتر على آخرين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas attributes to the Prophet the statement that the Greatest Name, by which God answers supplication, is in this verse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الجوزاء، عن ابن عباس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "اسم الله الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address includes all People of the Book, Jews, Christians, and those like them.
rows.anchor: هذا الخطاب يعم أهل الكتاب من اليهود والنصارى، ومن جرى مجراهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here kalima means a meaningful sentence, and sawa means justice and fairness in which both sides stand equally.
rows.anchor: والكلمة تطلق على الجملة المفيدة كما قال هاهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared call is to worship God alone and avoid every form of association, including idols, crosses, tyrants, fire, or anything else; all messengers preached this monotheism.
rows.anchor: لا وثنا، ولا صنما، ولا صليبا ولا طاغوتا، ولا نارا، ولا شيئا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Taking one another as lords means obeying one another in disobedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: يعني: يطيع بعضنا بعضا في معصية الله.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Taking one another as lords means some people prostrate to others.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: يعني: يسجد بعضنا لبعض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the People of the Book turn away from the fair invitation, believers should testify that they remain upon the Islam God legislated for them.
rows.anchor: فإن تولوا عن هذا النصف وهذه الدعوة فأشهدوهم أنتم على استمراركم على الإسلام

rows.speaker: أبو سفيان
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas's account of his audience with Heraclius, Abu Sufyan answered questions about Muhammad while still a polytheist; the meeting occurred after Hudaybiyya and before the conquest, and the Prophet's letter quoted this verse.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك بعد صلح الحديبية وقبل الفتح، كما هو مصرح به في الحديث

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others say the opening of Aal Imran through roughly eighty verses was revealed about the Najran delegation.
rows.anchor: أن صدر سورة آل عمران إلى بضع وثمانين آية منها نزلت في وفد نجران

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri says the Najran delegation were the first to offer jizya.
rows.anchor: وقال الزهري: هم أول من بذل الجزية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir raises the chronological tension between this verse's inclusion in the letter before the conquest and the report that the jizya verse came after it.
rows.anchor: فما الجمع بين كتابة هذه الآية قبل الفتح إلى هرقل في جملة الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible reconciliation is that this verse was revealed twice, once before Hudaybiyya and once after the conquest.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن هذه الآية نزلت مرتين، مرة قبل الحديبية، ومرة بعد الفتح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that the opening of Aal Imran through this verse concerned Najran, while this verse itself had already been revealed; the report extending the revelation to more than eighty verses may be unpreserved given Abu Sufyan's hadith.
rows.anchor: ليس بمحفوظ، لدلالة حديث أبي سفيان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reconciliation places the Najran delegation before Hudaybiyya and treats their payment as a settlement instead of jizya; the later jizya ruling then matched this precedent, as the shares ruling matched Abdullah ibn Jahsh's pre-Badr expedition.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن قدوم وفد نجران كان قبل الحديبية، وأن الذي بذلوه مصالحة عن المباهلة لا على وجه الجزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth possibility is that the Prophet ordered the wording in his letter before it was revealed, then revelation agreed with it, as it did with Umar's positions on the veil, captives, funeral prayer for hypocrites, and the Station of Abraham.
rows.anchor: كما نزل بموافقة عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه في الحجاب وفي الأسارى

rows.speaker: أبو رافع القرظي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas's report says that at a gathering of Jewish and Christian scholars from Najran, Abu Rafi asked whether Muhammad wanted them to worship him as Christians worship Jesus; a Najran Christian leader echoed the question.
rows.anchor: قال أبو رافع القرظي، حين اجتمعت الأحبار من اليهود والنصارى من أهل نجران، عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person granted scripture, judgment, and prophethood cannot tell people to worship him alongside God; if even a prophet cannot do so, no other person can all the more.
rows.anchor: ما ينبغي لبشر آتاه الله الكتاب والحكم والنبوة أن يقول للناس: اعبدوني من دون الله

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan says it is unsuitable for a believer to command people to worship him.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن البصري: لا ينبغي هذا لمؤمن أن يأمر الناس بعبادته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book served their rabbis and monks as lords by obeying them, as in the verse about taking religious authorities as lords.
rows.anchor: قال: وذلك أن القوم كان يعبد بعضهم بعضا -يعني أهل الكتاب- كانوا يتعبدون لأحبارهم ورهبانهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Adi ibn Hatim objected that people had not worshipped their religious authorities, the Prophet replied that they did so by obeying their declarations that the forbidden was lawful and the lawful forbidden.
rows.anchor: وفي المسند، والترمذي -كما سيأتي-أن عدي بن حاتم قال: يا رسول الله، ما عبدوهم. قال: "بلى، إنهم أحلوا لهم الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguided religious authorities are condemned, unlike messengers and practicing scholars who teach and prohibit only what God commanded; the messengers faithfully delivered their trust and counseled creation.
rows.anchor: فالجهلة من الأحبار والرهبان ومشايخ الضلال يدخلون في هذا الذم والتوبيخ، بخلاف الرسل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Abu Razin, and others explain rabbaniyyun as people who are wise, learned, and forbearing.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأبو رزين وغير واحد، أي: حكماء علماء حلماء.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan and others interpret rabbaniyyun as jurists; this is also reported from Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada, Ata al-Khurasani, Atiyya al-Awfi, and al-Rabi ibn Anas.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وغير واحد: فقهاء، وكذا روي عن ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، وقتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan also explains rabbaniyyun as people devoted to worship and piety.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أيضا: يعني أهل عبادة وأهل تقوى.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says anyone who learns the Quran must become learned in its jurisprudence, understanding its meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك في قوله: {بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب وبما كنتم تدرسون} حق على من تعلم القرآن أن يكون فقيها:

rows.speaker: قراءة بالتشديد
rows.claim: An alternative reading vocalizes taallamuna with a doubled letter, meaning that they teach the Book.
rows.anchor: وقرئ {تعلمون} بالتشديد من التعليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about studying the Book means memorizing its wording.
rows.anchor: تدرسون} تحفظون (10) ألفاظه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger does not command worship of angels, prophets, or anyone besides God; such a call is unbelief, whereas prophets call people to faith and worship of God alone.
rows.anchor: لأن من دعا إلى عبادة غير الله فقد دعا إلى الكفر، والأنبياء إنما يأمرون بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who acts for worldly reward receives what God apportioned here but no share in the afterlife; one seeking the afterlife receives it along with his worldly allotment.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن له في الآخرة [من] (1) نصيب، ومن قصد بعمله الدار الآخرة أعطاه الله منها مع ما قسم له في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will reward the grateful with His favor and mercy in this world and the next according to their gratitude and deeds.
rows.anchor: سنُعطيهم من فضلنا ورحمتنا في الدنيا والآخرة بحسب شكرهم وعملهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage consoles Muslims for what they felt on the day of Uhud.
rows.anchor: مسليا للمسلمين (2) عما كان وقع في نفوسهم يوم أحد

rows.speaker: الذين قرؤوا قتل معه
rows.claim: Readers of qutil understood that the prophet and some, but not all, of his companions were killed, leaving survivors who did not waver or weaken.
rows.anchor: فإنهم قالوا: إنما عنى بالقتل النبي وبعض من معه من الربيين دون جميعهم

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir argues against qātala: if they had been killed, saying afterward that they did not waver or weaken would make little sense.
rows.anchor: لو قتلوا (3) لم يكن لقوله: {فما وهنوا} وجه معروف

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers qutila because the passage rebukes those who fled at Uhud, abandoned fighting, or heard the cry that Muhammad had been killed, asking whether they would then turn back.
rows.anchor: ثم اختار قراءة من قرأ {قتل معه ربيون كثير} ؛ لأن الله [تعالى] (4) عاتب بهذه الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says many prophets were killed in front of their numerous companions.
rows.anchor: وكم من نبي قتل بين يديه من أصحابه ربيون كثير

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq reads the verse as a prophet being killed while many groups remained with him; they did not lose resolve after him, weaken against the enemy, or surrender in struggle for God and His religion.
rows.anchor: وكلام ابن إسحاق في السيرة يقتضي قولا آخر، [فإنه] (8) قال: أي وكأين من نبي

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli strongly supports Ibn Ishaq's reading, which fits the statement that the groups did not waver after what befell them; al-Ummawi also transmits this interpretation from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim's book.
rows.anchor: وقد نصر هذا القول السهيلي وبالغ فيه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud explains rabbiyyun as thousands.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود {ربيون كثير} أي: ألوف.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrima, Hasan, Qatada, al-Suddi, al-Rabi, and Ata al-Khurasani define rabbiyyun as large groups.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير، وعكرمة، والحسن، وقتادة، والسدي، والربيع، وعطاء الخراساني: الربيون: الجموع الكثيرة.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan explains rabbiyyun as many scholars, and elsewhere as patient, righteous, and pious scholars.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن: {ربيون كثير} أي: علماء كثير، وعنه أيضا: علماء صبر أبرار أتقياء.

rows.speaker: بعض نحاة البصرة
rows.claim: Some Basran grammarians say rabbiyyun are people who worship the Lord; an unnamed critic objects that this would require the form rabbiyyun with an open initial ra.
rows.anchor: أن الربيين هم الذين يعبدون الرب، عز وجل، قال: ورد بعضهم عليه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says rabbiyyun are followers and subjects, while rabbabiyyun are governors.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: "الربيون: الأتباع، والرعية، والربابيون: (1) الولاة.

rows.speaker: قتادة والربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Rabi ibn Anas say they were not weakened by their prophet's killing and did not abandon his support or religion, but fought for his cause until they met God.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة والربيع بن أنس: {وما ضعفوا} بقتل نبيهم {وما استكانوا} يقول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets istakānū as becoming humbled.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس {وما استكانوا} تخشعوا.

rows.speaker: السدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd interpret istakānū as not becoming humiliated before their enemy.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي وابن زيد: وما ذلوا لعدوهم.

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق وقتادة والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq, Qatada, and al-Suddi say what befell them did not occur when their prophet was killed.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق، وقتادة والسدي: أي ما أصابهم ذلك حين قتل نبيهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their constant prayer was to ask God to forgive their sins and excesses, steady their feet, and give them victory over unbelievers.
rows.anchor: لم يكن لهم هجيرى إلا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave them victory, success, and the good reward of the afterlife; He loves those who do good.
rows.anchor: أي: النصر والظفر والعاقبة (2) {وحسن ثواب الآخرة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through the prophets, God covenanted with the People of the Book to believe in Muhammad, announce him publicly so people would be ready, and follow him when sent.
rows.anchor: أخذ عليهم العهد على ألسنة الأنبياء أن يؤمنوا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأن ينوهوا بذكره في الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They concealed the covenant and exchanged the promised good of this world and the next for a small, contemptible worldly gain—a vile bargain.
rows.anchor: فكتموا ذلك وتعوضوا عما وعدوا عليه من الخير في الدنيا والآخرة بالدون الطفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage warns scholars against copying them and facing their punishment; scholars must share beneficial knowledge that guides good action and conceal none of it.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا تحذير للعلماء أن يسلكوا مسلكهم فيصيبهم ما أصابهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith transmitted through multiple routes says that whoever is asked for knowledge and conceals it will be bridled with fire on the Day of Resurrection; Ibn Kathir gives no grading.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "من سئل عن علم فكتمه ألجم يوم القيامة بلجام من نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir applies the verse to ostentatious people who boast of what they were not given and seek praise for deeds they never did.
rows.anchor: يعني بذلك المرائين المتكثرين بما لم يعطوا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report in both Sahih collections, a person making a false claim to increase his standing gains only further scarcity.
rows.anchor: من ادعى دعوى كاذبة ليتكثر بها لم يزده الله إلا قلة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in Sahih compares someone pretending to possess what he was not given to a person wearing two garments of falsehood.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيح: "المتشبع (4) بما لم يعط كلابس ثوبي زور"

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas answers Marwan that this passage concerns the People of the Book, not everyone who feels pleased and likes praise; they concealed the Prophet's answer and gave him a different one, then left implying they had answered and sought his praise for it.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: سألهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن شيء، فكتموه (11) وأخبروه بغيره

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that hypocritical men stayed behind when the Prophet went on a campaign, rejoiced at missing it, then made excuses and swore upon his return while seeking praise for what they had not done; Bukhari transmits this as a reason for revelation.
rows.anchor: أن رجالا من المنافقين على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الغزو تخلفوا عنه
